From: Helena Sanders <helena.sanders@helioshealth.com>

Cc: procurement@helioshealth.com

Subject: RFP: audit log handback requirements - Helios

Hi Karthik,

As part of our compliance track for the upcoming SOC3 assessment we need a detailed response to a few audit-log exportability/retention questions. We are collecting answers to include in our RFP package. Please see the list below — ideally we need a written response and a sample manifest by next Tuesday (2027-04-06).

1) Immutable timestamps: Do exported audit bundles include cryptographic verification (HMAC/PKI) or signed manifests that demonstrate a timeline (server-side monotonic timestamp + signature)? If so, provide the algorithm, key custody model, and verification steps.
2) Snapshot consistency: If we request an extract for a given time range, what guarantees do you provide that the export represents a consistent snapshot across services (auth, audit, events) and how are partial/in-flight writes handled?
3) Retention windows & legal holds: What are default retention periods for audit logs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments? How do you support customer-initiated legal holds or export freezes?
4) Export formats & delivery: What formats are available (NDJSON, Parquet, etc.), and what delivery mechanisms (S3 presigned, encrypted transfer appliance, physical media) do you support? Include max file sizes and recommended chunking.
5) Chain-of-custody / handback: Do you provide a documented chain-of-custody manifest and tamper-evidence (checksums + signing)? If a customer needs a notarized export, what is the process and lead time?
6) Redaction & PII handling: For exports that include user identifiers, what redaction/obfuscation options exist and how are they documented in the manifest?

We also ask for a sample export manifest and preferred schema. If there are constraints for on-prem vs hosted customers, call them out.

Thanks,
Helena
Senior Compliance Manager
Helios Health

Laura / Steph — forwarding Helena's request. Draft below are the responses I think are safe to send with a couple of open items for Steph. Please edit and sign off. We'll send the final from Laura to keep it authoritative.

--- DRAFT RESPONSES ---
1) Immutable timestamps / signatures:
- We generate a manifest for every export that contains: export_id, start_timestamp (ISO8601), end_timestamp, file checksums (SHA256), and a manifest_signature. For Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS / CloudHSM) to sign the manifest via an HMAC-SHA256 scheme; the signing key never leaves the HSM. For Hosted customers we sign with Redwood internal signing keys and provide a verification package (public verification key + signed timestamp certificate). Verification steps are: (a) compute SHA256 of each file, (b) verify the checksums match manifest, (c) verify manifest_signature using provided public key.
- Open item for Steph: confirm whether we also include a monotonic sequence counter across exports for additional ordering guarantees.

2) Snapshot consistency:
- Exports are based on a coordinated snapshot token minted by the orchestration layer at export time. The token ensures a consistent point-in-time view across auth, audit, and event stores. In-flight writes are handled by commit-time ordering: only events persisted before the snapshot token mint are included. For long-running exports we provide a "snapshot fence" in the manifest indicating truncation points; incremental exports include the parent_export_id to allow stitching.

3) Retention & legal hold:
- Defaults: Hosted = 3 years, Dedicated/Private configurable at provisioning (default 3, up to 7 contractual).
- Legal hold: customers can request an export freeze / legal hold via Console or API; we mark affected datasets as "no-delete" and surface the hold in the manifest. For Hosted customers we require authorization from the contract owner but will place holds upon signed request.

4) Formats & delivery:
- Formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) recommended for streaming/consumption; Parquet available for analytics exports.
- Delivery: S3 presigned URLs (configurable expiry, default 7 days), encrypted multipart transfer (TLS + server-side AES-256 encryption), or physical encrypted appliance for bulk (>10 TB) shipments. We recommend chunking files to 5GB objects for reliability.

5) Chain-of-custody / notarization:
- We produce a manifest with checksums and signatures and retain an audit trail of all export actions in our audit log for the duration of retention. For notarized exports we coordinate with a third-party notary (standard lead time ~10 business days) — commercial terms apply.

6) Redaction / PII handling:
- Exports can be produced in raw or redacted modes. Redaction options: deterministic hashing of identifiers, tokenization, or field-level redaction. The manifest indicates which redaction policy was applied and includes a redaction_version id.

Open items for Steph: default presigned URL expiry and whether we include export sequence counters. Also Laura: please review the notarization paragraph and contract language on KMS custody for Dedicated customers.

Thanks,
Karthik

Helena — thanks for the thorough list. Apologies for the small delay; we've compiled a concise RFP-style response and attached a sample manifest and export runbook. Summary answers below, followed by action items.

1) Immutable timestamps / signatures
- What we provide: Every export bundle includes a manifest (NDJSON metadata) with: export_id, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, per-file SHA256 checksums, export_sequence_number, and manifest_signature.
- Signing model:
  * Dedicated/Private: optional customer-managed key (AWS KMS or CloudHSM). We sign the manifest using HMAC-SHA256 where the key is stored in the customer's HSM/KMS. The customer retains key custody and can independently verify signatures.
  * Hosted: Redwood signs manifests with our internal signing key; we publish the corresponding verification key and an export-certificate package for verification.
- Verification steps: compute SHA256 per file, match checksums to manifest, verify manifest_signature using provided public key. We include a signature verification helper script in the runbook.

2) Snapshot consistency
- Guarantee: Exports are created from a coordinated snapshot token that represents a point-in-time across subsystem boundaries. Only records committed prior to token issuance are included.
- Long-running exports: We surface "snapshot_fence" markers and parent_export_id to allow consumers to rehydrate a consistent timeline; incremental exports are stitchable using those fields.

3) Retention windows & legal holds
- Defaults: Hosted = 3 years. Dedicated/Private = configurable at setup; contractual extension up to 7 years.
- Legal hold: Customers may request a legal hold through Console/API; upon validated request we mark datasets as immutable and do not allow deletion until hold release. The manifest records hold_id and requester.

4) Export formats & delivery options
- Formats: NDJSON (default), Parquet (columnar analytics), CSV for selected tables.
- Delivery options: S3 presigned URLs (default expiry 7 days; configurable), secure multipart TLS upload, SFTP over a customer gateway, or encrypted physical appliance for >10 TB. We recommend chunk sizes of 5 GB and provide MD5/SHA256 per chunk.

5) Chain-of-custody / notarization
- We provide a chain-of-custody section in the manifest listing: actor, timestamp, action (export_created/export_transferred/verified), and checksums.
- Notarization: We work with third-party notaries on request; typical lead time is ~10 business days and requires an SOW.

6) Redaction & PII handling
- Modes: raw, hashed-identifiers (deterministic), tokenized (reversible with customer KMS), or full redaction. The manifest records the redaction_policy and redaction_version.

Attachments included: handback-manifest-hel-20270405.pdf (sample manifest), export-runbook-ndjson-20270405.txt (verification scripts + runbook).

Action items:
- Steph: confirm default presigned URL expiry (we propose keeping default at 7 days but can extend to 30 days for Helios).
- Helena: if you want notarization we will scope an SOW and provide cost/lead-time; please confirm whether Helios requires an isolated on-prem export or is okay with an encrypted appliance shipment.
- Karthik: please add any KMS/sequence counter notes if needed.

If helpful, we can schedule a technical handoff call with our infra team to walk your engineers through the verification steps and runbook.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
